result.rationale: The diff confirms the mechanism: post.rb cook() returns raw verbatim when cook_method == raw_html (bypassing the markdown/sanitize pipeline); poll_feed.rb passes i.content from the configured feed into TopicEmbed.import → PostCreator with cook_method: raw_html and skip_validations: true; embed/best.html.erb renders `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. No sanitization of feed HTML appears anywhere in the diff, so stored XSS from a malicious feed is a real security defect introduced by this change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a code path where untrusted HTML is persisted and rendered without sanitization. `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim when `cook_method == :raw_html` (app/models/post.rb), and `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). The scheduled feed job pulls `i.content` from an external RSS/Atom feed and passes it into `TopicEmbed.import` with only `CGI.unescapeHTML`/`scrub` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb), i.e., no HTML sanitization. The embed view renders it using `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), and since `post.cooked == post.raw` for raw_html posts, this is a stored XSS vector if the feed is malicious/compromised.
